result.summary: Replaces container-specific removal idioms, such as the vector erase-remove idiom and list member removal, with C++20's std::erase and std::erase_if across 13 files. It also updates several simple iterator-based erase calls to use the standard free functions.
result.problem: Legacy erase patterns differ across container types: array-based containers require the two-step erase-remove idiom which is error-prone if the erase step or end iterator is mishandled, whereas node-based containers use member removal. This inconsistency leads to verbose and potentially bug-prone container mutation code.
evidence: PR description notes that omitting the erase call or the end iterator in the erase-remove idiom can introduce bugs (citing clang-tidy's bugprone-inaccurate-erase and discussion in #36588).
result.scope_notes: Mechanical modernization across multiple files adopting C++20 container utilities.
result.card: This pull request converts container removal patterns across 13 files to C++20 std::erase and std::erase_if. The change replaces the verbose and error-prone vector erase-remove idiom and container-specific removal methods with uniform standard library functions. The author notes that manual erase-remove idioms risk subtle bugs like forgetting to invoke erase or passing incorrect iterators, citing prior review discussion in PR 36588.
uncertainties: Diff and file list were omitted, so the exact subsystems and containers touched cannot be verified.

risk.why: A faulty predicate or incorrect element erasure could inadvertently retain or drop container elements, causing logic bugs in the affected components.
